sentences.text: Yamatosaurus is a basal hadrosaurid dinosaur, a member of the duck-billed group, from the Late Cretaceous. The genus contains only one known species, Yamatosaurus izanagii.
Its fossils were found in marine sediments deposited on the edge of a continental slope in an intra-arc basin, a surprising location for such a dinosaur.

Shingo Kishimoto discovered the holotype—the specimen the species is based on—on Awaji Island in Japan in May 2004. The discovery was first reported in scientific literature in 2005. The holotype was donated to a museum in Hyogo Prefecture in 2013 and formally described in 2021 after preparation by Kazumi Wada, Tomomi Ikeda, and Chisato Ota. Yamatosaurus izanagii was named in 2021 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Ryuji Takasaki, Katsuhiro Kubota, and Anthony Ricardo Fiorillo.

Yamatosaurus lived during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous; while some estimates place its range at approximately 71.94 to 71.69 million years ago, other estimates suggest a broader time range from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that Yamatosaurus coexisting with the more derived Kamuysaurus indicates a level of provinciality in hadrosaur evolution.
